headline: Your work is making news. Let's make it easier to share.
intro: From the Twitty Park lawsuit to Georgia's first Superfund Research Center, 2026 has been a big year for GEC. Your website is in good shape, so I'm not going to pitch you a new one. Instead, I'd help your team turn every announcement and technical report into steady, plain-language posts without adding hours to anyone's week.
working: An up-to-date events calendar with RSVP links
Press releases and news coverage posted regularly
Clear ways to act: report air problems, donate, volunteer
Named staff and board, and a story that goes back to 1990

findings.title: Big news arrives in bursts.
findings.detail: Nine of this year's 13 news items came out in a single week in June, around the Superfund Research Center announcement. Each one could have become a week of posts, a newsletter story and an explainer.

findings.title: The Superfund page doesn't name the sites.
findings.detail: It says Glynn County is home to 4 of Georgia's 16 Superfund sites, but doesn't name them or link to any reports, just as the new research center is drawing attention to them.

findings.title: Technical topics need plain language.
findings.detail: Air quality, seafood safety and Superfund cleanups come with dense EPA and EPD documents. AI tools can draft plain-language summaries for your team to check, so more residents understand what's at stake.

findings.title: The LinkedIn icon goes nowhere.
findings.detail: It appears on every page with no link. Linking your LinkedIn page or removing the icon is a two-minute fix in Wix, and I'm glad to show you how at no charge.

images.caption: What the press-release tool would produce: four drafts from one announcement, ready for your team to review.

outcome: Two AI tools set up for your team, plus a one-hour training. One turns each press release, report or event into ready-to-review social posts and a newsletter story. The other drafts plain-language explainers from technical documents. Your staff reviews everything before it's published, and nothing confidential goes in.
timeline: About 2 weeks from kickoff, including the training session.

package.note: A press-release-to-posts assistant and a plain-language explainer assistant, set up with your voice, your facts and your review steps, plus a 1-hour team training and a written how-to guide.

addons.note: I write and schedule 8 posts a month on 2 platforms from your news and events, so your team only has to approve them.
Make sure your Google listing, Facebook and Instagram all share the same up-to-date information and links.
